theory_object.title: Fundamental Information Analysis
mechanisms: fundamental signals may contain incremental information about earnings persistence and value relevance
theory_object.claim_boundary: Information content for selected signals is not a universal causal driver ontology and requires sector/regime retesting.

theory_object.title: Ratio Analysis and Equity Valuation: From Research to Practice
mechanisms: hierarchical ratio analysis separates operating and financing activities and decomposes higher-level payoff drivers
theory_object.claim_boundary: Hierarchical decomposition is an analytical and forecasting architecture, not causal identification and not sector invariant.

theory_object.title: Accounting Earnings and Cash Flows as Measures of Firm Performance: The Role of Accounting Accruals
mechanisms: accruals can mitigate cash-flow timing and matching noise in performance measurement
theory_object.claim_boundary: Cash flow is not automatically superior to accrual earnings; divergence requires operating-cycle and working-capital context.

theory_object.title: Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows About Future Earnings?
mechanisms: accrual and cash-flow components can differ in future earnings persistence
theory_object.claim_boundary: Sample evidence on persistence and pricing is not a fraud diagnostic or universal live mispricing rule.

theory_object.title: Agency Costs, Net Worth, and Business Fluctuations
mechanisms: borrower net worth affects external-finance agency cost and can amplify investment fluctuations
theory_object.claim_boundary: Balance-sheet transmission requires borrower-channel evidence; aggregate credit correlation alone is insufficient causal evidence.

theory_object.title: Credit Cycles
mechanisms: collateral values and borrowing limits can create persistent credit and asset-price feedback when constraints bind
theory_object.claim_boundary: The feedback requires collateralized borrowing and binding constraints and cannot be inferred from simple credit-price correlation.

theory_object.title: Capital Asset Prices: A Theory of Market Equilibrium under Conditions of Risk
mechanisms: required return reflects time value and compensation for priced systematic risk under equilibrium assumptions
theory_object.claim_boundary: Restrictive assumptions prevent CAPM from serving as a universal discount-rate or target-price engine.

theory_object.title: The Dividend-Price Ratio and Expectations of Future Dividends and Discount Factors
mechanisms: present-value relations decompose valuation ratios into expected cash-flow growth and discount-rate components
theory_object.claim_boundary: Model decomposition is not unique causal identification and does not confer market-timing authority.

theory_object.title: Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading
mechanisms: market depth and price impact are distinct microstructure dimensions of liquidity
theory_object.claim_boundary: Model depth is not equivalent to realized stress-exit capacity across market structures or funding states.

theory_object.title: Market Liquidity and Funding Liquidity
mechanisms: market liquidity and funding liquidity can reinforce each other through margin and funding constraints
theory_object.claim_boundary: The stress mechanism requires funding and margin observables; normal-state ADV or spread alone is insufficient.

theory_object.title: Determinants of Portfolio Performance
mechanisms: portfolio performance can be decomposed relative to policy benchmark into allocation timing and selection effects
theory_object.claim_boundary: Attribution is benchmark- and question-dependent and is not unique causal explanation of realized P&L.

theory_object.title: A Variance Decomposition for Stock Returns
mechanisms: unexpected equity returns can be decomposed into future cash-flow news and expected-return news under a present-value VAR framework
theory_object.claim_boundary: Model-based news decomposition does not identify a unique real-world causal event and must preserve residual/model uncertainty.
